analyst_view.overall: Early view: Santa Clara are 4th with one of the best defences in the league (8 conceded), but Record reports a wave of absences: Guilherme Romão, Pedro Ferreira and Tiago Ferreira are injured, and Pedro Pacheco (sent off against Gil Vicente) and Emanuel Moreira (fifth yellow) are suspended for this very match. Moreirense are 9th under Vasco Botelho da Costa, lost only 1-0 at Sporting, and hope the long break brings back Francisco Domingues and Kiko Bondoso from muscle injuries.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals. I lean slightly higher: Moreirense's games have averaged close to three goals (13 scored, 18 conceded), and Santa Clara arrive without two suspended players and three injured ones. A depleted visiting side makes it harder to keep the usual tight Santa Clara game.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners, split evenly. Santa Clara usually keep the ball, as Petit said of the Gil Vicente defeat, while Moreirense want to press higher at home; those effects roughly cancel out. I stay with the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, already a high figure. Santa Clara come in with two players banned, one a red card, and Petit complained about a flurry of second-half yellows against Gil Vicente, so they are not a calm side. Without a named referee I see no reason to push beyond the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.6 shots. I lean higher: Botelho da Costa has said he wants Moreirense to press higher, and they were 3-0 up at half-time at Estoril recently. Santa Clara create a lot through possession but, as Petit admitted, have not been finishing well, which tends to mean more attempts.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 6.3 shots on target, which looks low for two sides that have scored 13 and 16. With Santa Clara's back line short of bodies, Moreirense should get more clean looks than usual. I would put it closer to 7.
